about: The target kernel set of a plain decode step of the dense Qwen 3.5-architecture model: per block call of a step the kernel a stack that reproduces the set launches, in step order.

kernels: per kernel id what it is, where it comes from and how it stands to the target -- 'target' of kind 'code' (the target's own compiled kernel: an entry, a library call or a framework operator called as the target calls it) or of kind 'port' (a kernel whose home is cuDNN Frontend: an entry that reproduces the target kernel's results byte for byte), or 'stand-in' (a declared replacement for an operation that lives inside a serving engine). 'entry' is null until a stack of this repository calls an entry for the kernel; with an entry comes 'form', what the target passes to it.

A port's byte equality is the entry's own record, not a measurement of the sample that reads this file: 'tie_out' says where that comparison stands and on which GPU class it was made, 'differences' what differs from the target's kernel besides its results. A port without an entry here has neither yet.

configurations: per GPU class and SM count one section. 'geometry' is the layer widths of the model the section holds for; a model with other widths has no section. 'launch' is [grid, block, shared memory in bytes] of one launch at the section's row count; 'at' names further fields of the geometry that one launch shape was recorded with. A section is 'recorded' (launch records of the target on that class) or 'planned' (derived, never claimed); 'claimed' is false until a stack launches every kernel of the section.

The numbers of a section are three, never one: of its launches per step, how many are the target's own compiled kernels (code), how many cuDNN Frontend entries with byte-equal results (port), how many declared stand-ins. They count what a complete stack launches: a port is counted whether or not its entry is called by a stack yet.
A change of a form this file names changes this file in the same commit.

cublaslt_fp8_gemm.selection: the library's tuner chooses the kernel: a pick is recorded and never gated, so no launch shape is held here

attention_prepare.what: attention preparation: norm, rotary embedding, cache insert

fi_decode_attention.what: attention core over a paged cache

gate_quant.tie_out: Compared when the entry was written: its output bytes against the target kernel's for every pair of bf16 operand values, at 14 scales, on compute capability 10.3 -- no differing byte. No such comparison is recorded for compute capability 10.0. It needs the target's kernel and is not a test of this repository. In the repository: the entry's numerics contract (docs/operations/attention/gate_quant_decode.md) and its suites (test/python/attention_gate/frost/).
differences: a kernel of its own: the same arithmetic at the same rounding points in another instruction stream than the target kernel's

swiglu_fp4.what: MLP gate / up multiply with SiLU x up and the 4-bit quantise

fi_fp4_quantize.what: 4-bit quantise of the final hidden rows in front of the output head
